chunks: When Allah spoke intimately to Mūsā ibn ʿImrān [upon our Prophet and] upon him السلام, Mūsā said: “My Lord, are You far from me so that I should call upon You, or are You near so that I may converse with You?”
So Allah, Majestic is His Glory, revealed to him:
“I am the companion of the one who remembers Me.”
Then Mūsā عليه السلام said: “My Lord, I am in circumstances in which I regard You too reverently to mention You in them.”
He said: “O Mūsā, remember Me in every state.”

key_terms.أَحْوَالٍ: states or circumstances a person may be in
key_terms.جَلِيسُ: companion or close presence with the one who remembers Allah
key_terms.رَبِّ: My Lord, addressing Allah with devotion

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith teach that Allah should be remembered in every state?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah is near to the one who remembers Him, and that dhikr is not restricted to select moments only. It emphasizes that one should remember Allah in every condition, making constant remembrance a sign of reverence and nearness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.58 - When Allah (swt) spoke to Musa ibn Imran (as),
Musa (as) asked: "O’ Lord (azj), are You far from me that I should call to You, or are You near that I may converse with You?"
Allah (swt), Glorious and Exalted, revealed to him:
"I am with the one who remembers Me. "
Musa (as) then said: "O’ Lord (azj), there are circumstances in which I hold You in such reverence that I would not mention You."
Allah (swt) said: "O’ Musa, remember Me in all circumstances."
